sources.title: 70thNationalFilmAwardsfortheyear2022announced
claims: Daman won Best Odia Film at the 70th National Film Awards for 2022, announced on 16 August 2024.
The named recipients are producer JP Motion Pictures and directors Vishal Mourya and Debi Prasad Lenka.
limits: This was a language-category film award, not the overall Best Feature Film award or a Best Actor award.

sources.title: 70thNationalFilmAwards catalogue
claims: 121 minutes. Directors: Vishal Mourya and Debi Prasad Lenka. Producer: JP Motion Pictures. Editor: Debi Prasad Lenka. Cinematographer: Pratap Rout. Sound designer: Tusar Jena.
The official synopsis sets the story in 2015: Dr Siddharth is assigned to a remote Malkangiri primary health centre and works to combat malaria despite difficult conditions.
The catalogue connects the film with Durgama Anchalre Malaria Nirakarana, targeting malaria in inaccessible areas.
Director biographies identify Biju Babu (2019) and B for Bundelkhand (2017); Mourya studied engineering.
limits: The synopsis describes a film story, not measured health outcomes.
Promotional terms such as blockbuster are not verified box-office data.
No reusable licence established for catalogue stills.

sources.title: OdishaHealthandFamilyWelfareAnnualActivityReport2016–17
claims: DAMaN supplements routine malaria control in inaccessible villages and hamlets of high-endemic districts.
The report describes screening symptomatic and asymptomatic cases, vector control using LLIN and IRS, and nutritional and haemoglobin monitoring for vulnerable groups.
It plans camps before and after the monsoon, initially in eight districts, with extension planned for 2017–18.
Rs 10 crore was approved for financial year 2016–17.
limits: This historical plan is not proof that every activity occurred or a statement of current medical guidance.
Do not use the film’s 2015 setting as evidence of the actual programme’s launch date.
Do not attribute the real programme or all malaria reduction to a single heroic doctor.

sources.title: Daman(Dubbed)Review
claims: The review identifies Babushaan Mohanty as Dr Siddharth and Dipanwit Dashmohapatra as pharmacist Ravindra.
It praises performances and direction while criticising the screenplay’s pace and engagement.
It records the Hindi-dubbed release on 3 February 2023 through Panorama Studios in Bombay cinemas.
limits: One trade review of the Hindi dub, not audience consensus.
Its commercial forecast is not box-office evidence.

editorial_opportunities: Explain the 2022 award year versus the 2024 announcement.
Make co-direction and Lenka’s editing credit visible.
Distinguish the dramatised doctor’s commitment from the real programme’s collective work.
Describe mixed Hindi-dub criticism without claiming universal acclaim.
exclusions: No full-film viewing: do not invent scenes or dialogue.
No verified exact biographical identification of Dr Siddharth with Dr Omkar Hota.
No verified global festival prize or box-office return.
Distinct from Kalpana Lajmi’s 2001 Hindi film Daman.
